content:Speaker user says: Given the text: As an agency based in South Louisiana, we know a thing or two about festivals. (Our weekend calendars are essentially centered around them.) So for us, it’s no surprise more and more Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) brands are turning to festivals as lucrative opportunities to launch new products, build brand recognition and gain new consumers.
Of all the D2C sectors out there, the food industry is first in line when it comes to taking full advantage of the festival scene and its perks. After all, niche audience targeting coupled with in-person interactions makes for the perfect storm of product bliss. In fact, these annual events have become reliable advertising hubs for companies, celebrating everything from champagne to roadkill cuisine (yes, really).
So how is the playing field different for foodies? Broad spectrum access. While non-food brands have to sift through festival lists looking for an applicable fit for their product, food brands have a pretty large market to choose from. After all, who’s going to turn down free food?
Then, of course, we have the specialty festivals. These product-focused celebrations draw crowds of consumers interested in engaging with and testing out new brands for particular products. Some of them attend simply because they’re curious, with no previous preferences. Others enter the mix for their love of the product, looking to challenge their own brand loyalties.
This lucrative marketing scheme isn’t necessarily exclusive, either. We’re living in a time where you can name just about any type of food or drink, and there’s probably a festival for it. And if there’s a festival for it, you better believe people will show up. In the industry, we call this “your audience.” They’re right there, standing in front of your rickety booth table ready to taste goods and decide for themselves.
If you’re a major brand, these festivals could be the perfect moment for a big product reveal. If you’re a small company or startup, this is your chance to prove your product against its heavyweight competitors. You know the old adage: Give a man your product, make him a consumer for life (or something like that).
When it comes to shining examples, New York City’s Pinknic comes to mind. Relatively new to the city festival scene, Pinknic is held every summer and draws in thousands to Governor’s Island. As its name suggests, this celebration is all about pink — specifically in the bubbly form known as rosé.
What’s so great about the festival’s setup is not the breadth in product they have to offer (even though their stock is pretty impressive). It’s the lifestyle surrounding rosé that they’ve captured so well. Their consumers are anything but standard. And this isn’t just some run-of-the-mill booth stroll.
Festival goers, decked in the mandatory dress code of pink and white, enjoy bottles upon bottles of various rosés as they lounge by glittering pools or sunbathe to the musical stylings of a handpicked act. Crépes and main courses from NYC’s finest are served around the clock, along with chill vibes and ferris wheel rides. Why? Because rosé is about indulgence, and by extension, so is its audience.
Since its inception in 2016, Pinknic has been featured in publications like Vogue, Marie Claire, Thrillist, InStyle, The New York Times and more.
The real reason why festival marketing is so effective? Because it flips the common marketing scheme on its head. Rather than meeting consumers where they are, brands are now taking advantage of this ever-evolving experiential marketing canvas to bring audiences to them. And as Pinknic proves, crafting a festival to the lifestyle of your consumer group is a great way to connect the right people with the right product.

content:Speaker assistant says: Powerboats and sailboats are two types of watercraft that differ in their propulsion systems and design. Here are their differences and pros and cons:

1. Propulsion

- Powerboats use motors to propel the boat forward while sailboats use the wind and sails to move.

2. Design

- Powerboats have sleek and aerodynamic designs that are optimized for speed, while sailboats have larger hulls and masts to catch the wind and maneuverability.

3. Operating costs

- Powerboats require fuel and regular maintenance, which can be costly. Sailboats do not require fuel but may require periodic maintenance on their rigging and sails.

4. Speed

- Powerboats can travel faster than sailboats in calm waters. Sailboats depend on wind conditions and may be slower in calm or adverse conditions.

5. Navigation

- Powerboats can navigate in any direction, even against the wind, while sailboats require favorable wind conditions to travel in a specific direction.

6. Environmentally friendly

- While powerboats rely on fossil fuels, sailboats provide a more environmentally-friendly way to travel by harnessing the wind's energy.

Overall, the choice between a powerboat and a sailboat depends on personal preferences and usage. Powerboats are ideal for water sports, fishing, and transportation while sailboats are preferred for leisure, adventure, and sustainable travel. context:The content provides a comprehensive comparison of powerboats and sailboats, detailing their differences in propulsion, design, operating costs, speed, navigation capabilities, and environmental impact. keywords: powerboats, sailboats, propulsion tags: practical_sailing_tips, sustainable_living_strategies, boat_maintenance_and_safety, user_request_follow_up, improvement_planning, eco_friendly_practices, renewable_energy_integration, powerboat_sailboat_comparison, detailed_analysis

content:Speaker assistant says: There are various types of boats used for recreational activities, and they differ from each other based on their purposes, features, and designs. Some of the common types of boats used for recreational activities include:

2. Pontoon boats: Pontoon boats are ideal for leisurely cruising and relaxing on the water. They are relatively large and stable, with a flat deck and a shallow draft, making them easy to maneuver in calm waters. They are suitable for activities such as fishing, swimming, and sunbathing.

3. Fishing boats: Fishing boats are specifically designed for fishing and are equipped with features such as fishing rods, live wells, and fish finders. They come in different sizes and designs, with some being small and compact for solo outings, while others are larger with cabins for overnight stays.

4. Sailboats: Sailboats rely on wind power for propulsion and are ideal for those who enjoy sailing and the thrill of the wind. They come in various sizes and designs, from small dinghies to large yachts, and are suitable for different levels of sailing experience.

5. Houseboats: Houseboats are floating homes that provide a comfortable and unique way to enjoy the water. They are usually large and spacious, with amenities such as bedrooms, living areas, kitchens, and bathrooms. They are ideal for long-term stays on the water and for exploring remote waterways.

Overall, the type of boat chosen for recreational activities will depend on the individual's needs and preferences, as well as the intended use and location of the boat. context:The content outlines five distinct categories of boats used for recreation, detailing their specific designs, purposes, and ideal activities while noting that the choice depends on individual needs and intended use. keywords: recreational activities, boat types, features and designs tags: recreational_boating, boat_classification, watercraft_types, recreational_activities, safety_considerations, general_boating_classes, classification_systems, recreational_vessels

content:Speaker user says: How can a business develop and perfect its SMaC Recipe and make necessary changes to it over time? Generate according to: What is a SMaC Recipe and Why Does Your Business Need One? Does your business have a well-defined operating code for turning your strategic concepts into reality? Does it have a set of practices more enduring than mere tactics that create a replicable and consistent formula for successful outcomes? Do your enduring practices force order amid chaos and impose consistency when slammed by disruption? This is how Jim Collins defines a SMaC Recipe in his book Great by Choice (SMaC stands for Specific, Methodical and Consistent). A few weeks ago, I posted about Ray Dalio’s model for business. In this model the “Machine” was responsible for turning vision and goals into outcomes. The Machine consists of people, processes and tools. A SMaC Recipe is the unique combination of people, processes and tools that turn the organization’s vision and goals into outcomes. It is the nerve center of the Machine and it controls how the Machine functions. Without a clearly defined SMaC Recipe your organization’s Machine will not produce the outcome that your vision is striving for. Your outcomes will be inconsistent and you will be unable to turn strategic concepts into reality. A SMaC Recipe is not created overnight. It takes time, effort, many tweaks and adjustments to build a recipe that is a correct fit for your marketplace and organization. It is not a simple thing to have a SMaC Recipe that delivers consistent business outcomes in line with your vision and goals. However, once you have this SMaC Recipe perfected, it should not be adjusted unless there are fundamental changes in your business or industry. Collins gives the example of the United States constitution as a great SMaC Recipe. Since the US constitution was ratified in 1791, until 2011, only 17 amendments were made to it. This is one change every 13 years. Think of all the tumultuous and mind boggling change that has happened throughout that time period (in the US and in the world in general), yet this SMaC Recipe is still very close to what it was back in 1791 and has served the United States well over this time period. Spend some time this next week reviewing your business and asking questions like; What is your organization’s SMaC Recipe? Are you in the development stage or is your Recipe well defined? Is your SMaC Recipe producing the outcomes that are desired or does it need to be tweaked? I worked for a company with a well defined SMaC recipe. It was amazing and the business is flourishing. The CEO/CFO of the company introduced their recipe to us in a fun and exciting environment; the items on the list were reasonable, attainable, and easy to remember. Even though I no longer work for that company, I find myself referring back to that SMaC list for guidance. My current employer should thank them, and YOU for what I have learned! Excellent feedback Sarah! A properly define SMaC recipe can really transform a business. It’s sounds like your experience is a great example of this! context:This content outlines a five-step strategic framework for businesses to develop a SMaC Recipe, emphasizing long-term vision, process assessment, and iterative refinement to ensure consistency and sustained growth. keywords: SMaC Recipe, consistent outcomes, strategic concepts tags: business_strategy, smac_recipe_development, iterative_refinement, organizational_consistency

content:Speaker assistant says: So, how can a business develop and perfect its SMaC Recipe and make necessary changes to it over time?

1. Define your vision and goals: A clear and well-defined vision and goals are required to develop a SMaC Recipe that aligns with your organization's outcomes.

2. Collect data: Collect data from your internal and external stakeholders to understand the marketplace, the strengths and weaknesses of your organization, and your customer's needs.

3. Identify your unique combination of people, processes, and tools: Evaluate and identify those reliable and robust processes that have remained unchanged for a long period of time, the people that you can trust, and the tools that make you more efficient.

4. Write down your SMaC Recipe: Write down your SMaC Recipe, making sure it is a simple list that can be easily explained, understood, and remembered by everyone in your organization. It should be specific, methodical, and consistent.

5. Refine your SMaC Recipe: Continuously refine your SMaC Recipe to ensure it's still serving your vision and goals. Regularly revisit your Recipe to make sure it's still delivering consistent outcomes in line with your organization's objectives.

6. Make necessary changes: If fundamental changes occur in your business or industry, necessary changes to your SMaC Recipe may be required to stay aligned with your vision and goals.

Developing and perfecting your SMaC Recipe is not an easy feat, but it's worth the effort. It can create a replicable and consistent formula for success and force order amid chaos, positioning you to succeed despite industry disruptions. context:A business leader seeks practical examples on ensuring the consistent implementation and compliance of their SMaC Recipe across all staff members. keywords: SMaC Recipe, vision, goals, data, refine, changes, success tags: employee_engagement, compliance, implementation_strategy, business_strategy, smac_recipe_application, case_studies, competitive_analysis, industry_leaders, strategic_frameworks, southwest_airlines, toyota, mcdonalds, apple, amazon, business_success_stories

1. Define your long-term vision and goals: Your long-term goals will guide you as you develop your SMaC Recipe. They provide you with a framework of sustainability and continuity for your business.

2. Assess your current business processes: Take an honest look at the processes that would serve as the foundation for your SMaC Recipe. Identify the ones that have worked consistently over time, even in the face of disruptions.

3. Identify your special sauce: Reflect on the unique combination of people, processes, and tools that make up the core of your business. These are the things that could differentiate you from others in your industry.

4. Collect feedback: Gather feedback from employees and customers on what they think works well, and what doesn't. Use their feedback to inform the development of your SMaC Recipe, and continuously assess whether it's delivering consistent outcomes in line with your objectives.

5. Refine your SMaC Recipe: As you start to see what works and what doesn't, look for opportunities to improve your SMaC Recipe. Make adjustments where necessary to ensure that it continues to produce the desired outcomes.

Developing a SMaC Recipe is a continual process, and it takes time and effort; however, it results in consistency, reliability, and sustained growth. By taking these steps to develop your SMaC Recipe, you can create a replicable formula for success that will guide your business towards achieving long-term success. context:A speaker seeks advice on initiating and improving their SMaC Recipe formulation, specifically asking for tips for businesses unsure of where to start. keywords: SMaC Recipe, long-term vision, business processes, feedback, sustainability tags: business_strategy, smac_recipe_development, iterative_refinement, organizational_consistency, smac_recipe_examples, business_implementation_cases, beginner_guidance, strategic_frameworks, five_step_framework

content:Speaker assistant says: Certainly, here are some examples of how a business can ensure that its SMaC Recipe is consistent and adhered to by all employees:

1. Communicate your SMaC Recipe regularly: Make sure that your team understands your SMaC Recipe and how each factor contributes to the organization's success. Hold regular meetings to discuss how the Recipe is working, and make any necessary adjustments as you go.

2. Train your employees: Train all employees about your SMaC Recipe and how it fits into your organization's vision and goals. Explain the importance of the Recipe and how they can use it to guide their work.

3. Create a culture of accountability: Make it clear that all employees are responsible for upholding the SMaC Recipe. Empower them to speak up about any deviations from the Recipe and to make suggestions for improvements.

4. Create performance metrics: Use performance metrics that align with your SMaC Recipe to track employee performance. This will show employees how their work contributes to the organization's success and will help them to align their work with the Recipe.

5. Reward adherence to your SMaC Recipe: Recognize and reward employees who consistently adhere to your SMaC Recipe. This will motivate them to continue upholding the Recipe in their work.

content:Speaker assistant says: Some of the factors that influence the performance and maneuverability of racing sailboats are:

1. Hull shape: The design of the hull influences the speed and stability of the sailboat. A long and narrow hull is faster than a short and wide one, but the latter is more stable.

2. Sail area and rigging: The amount of sail area and the rigging setup affects the speed, maneuverability, and handling of the sailboat.

3. Weight and balance: The weight distribution and balance of the sailboat determine its stability and ability to sail smoothly in different conditions.

4. Keel and rudder design: The keel and rudder help to provide stability and control during sailing, and their design affects the performance and maneuverability of the sailboat.

Over time, racing sailboats have evolved significantly in their design and technology. Some of the key changes include:

1. The use of lighter materials and advanced composites like carbon fiber, which helps to reduce weight and increase speed.

2. Improved sail designs and rigging systems that allow for greater control and maneuverability.

3. The use of computer modeling and simulation to optimize sailboat design for different sailing conditions.

4. Advances in keel and rudder design, including the use of retractable and adjustable keels for improved performance in varying water depths.

5. The development of foiling technology, which allows the sailboat to lift above the water and reduce drag, resulting in higher speeds and greater maneuverability. context:The memory analyzes design factors and technological advancements in racing sailboats, including hull shapes, materials, and performance optimizations. keywords: racing sailboats, hull design, performance, maneuverability, technology, materials tags: racing_sailboats_performance_factors, racing_sailboats_technological_advancements, sailboat_hull_optimization, sailboat_material_innovation, design_priorities, research_impact, sailboat_design_priorities, simulation_techniques, crew_skill_importance, rigging_evolution

content:Speaker assistant says: Designers prioritize specific factors based on the type of racing and conditions the sailboat will encounter. For example, a sailboat designed for offshore racing in open ocean conditions may prioritize stability and safety over speed, whereas a sailboat designed for shorter courses or inshore racing may prioritize speed.

To decide which factors to prioritize over others, designers use computer modeling and tank testing to simulate and analyze different scenarios. These simulations factor in variables such as wind speed, water conditions, and the size of the racing crew to optimize the sailboat's performance.

Additionally, designers work closely with experienced racing sailors and teams to understand their needs and preferences. Based on this collaboration and testing, designers can identify critical design elements that will make the sailboat competitive and ensure its performance in different conditions.

Ultimately, the goal is to create a sailboat that is well-balanced and optimized for the specific type of racing, with no one factor prioritized over others so that the crew can achieve the best possible performance on the water. context:Sailboat designers utilize computer modeling, tank testing, and collaboration with racing teams to balance specific factors like stability and speed according to the intended racing environment. keywords: sailboat design, racing conditions, optimization tags: sailboat_design_priorities, design_collaboration, simulation_techniques, crew_boat_synergy

content:Speaker assistant says: Technology has greatly impacted the design of sailboat rigging, improving performance, durability, and safety. The use of CAD (computer-aided design) software has allowed for more precise and efficient designs. 

One significant change is the use of composite materials such as carbon fiber, Kevlar, and Dyneema. These materials are much lighter and stronger than traditional materials such as stainless steel, aluminum, and wire ropes. Using these composites in rigging results in less weight aloft, reducing the boat's center of gravity and increasing stability. 

Another significant change is the use of continuous rigging. Traditional rigging used a series of wire ropes, turnbuckles, and spreaders to support the mast and sails. Continuous rigging, however, uses a single piece of strong, multi-strand synthetic fiber, such as Dyneema, that runs continuously from the masthead to the deck. This results in a stronger and lighter rig, reducing wind-resistance and improving performance. 

In addition, technology has resulted in the development of better blocks, cleats, winches, and furling systems that allow for easier and more precise sail handling. 

Overall, technology has allowed for safer, lighter, and more efficient sailboat rigging by incorporating advanced materials and designs. context:This content explains how advanced materials like carbon fiber and Dyneema, along with continuous rigging systems, have revolutionized sailboat rigging by enhancing performance, durability, and safety. keywords: composite materials, continuous rigging, performance tags: sailboat_rigging_evolution, composite_materials_advancement, continuous_rigging_systems, CAD_design_application, performance_enhancement_techniques, safety_improvements

content:Speaker assistant says: Yes, these changes have made sailing more accessible for beginners. The use of composite materials and continuous rigging has made sailboats lighter and easier to handle. This means that even small sailboats can be more easily maneuvered by novice sailors. The better blocks, cleats, winches, and furling systems have also made it easier to adjust sails, and maneuver the boat in varying wind conditions. 

Furthermore, the use of CAD software has allowed for more precise and efficient designs, making sailboats easier to build and maintain. This has provided more opportunities for first-time sailors to get on the water without the hassle of complex rigging.

Additionally, advancements in safety have also made it easier for novices to get involved in sailing. content:Speaker assistant says: Powerboats and sailboats are two types of watercraft that differ in their propulsion systems and design. Here are their differences and pros and cons:

1. Propulsion

- Powerboats use motors to propel the boat forward while sailboats use the wind and sails to move.

2. Design

- Powerboats have sleek and aerodynamic designs that are optimized for speed, while sailboats have larger hulls and masts to catch the wind and maneuverability.

3. Operating costs

- Powerboats require fuel and regular maintenance, which can be costly. Sailboats do not require fuel but may require periodic maintenance on their rigging and sails.

4. Speed

- Powerboats can travel faster than sailboats in calm waters. Sailboats depend on wind conditions and may be slower in calm or adverse conditions.

5. Navigation

- Powerboats can navigate in any direction, even against the wind, while sailboats require favorable wind conditions to travel in a specific direction.

6. Environmentally friendly

- While powerboats rely on fossil fuels, sailboats provide a more environmentally-friendly way to travel by harnessing the wind's energy.

Overall, the choice between a powerboat and a sailboat depends on personal preferences and usage. content:Speaker user says: Given the text: Northwest Youth Sailing - Start Sailing!
Like other youth sports and activities, sailing is meant to be fun, empowering, and social. Sailing offers a unique medium to teach more than just practical skills. Sailing can offer tranquility, adventure, and excitement all in one day. Adversity and challenges along the way provide many opportunities for personal growth and teamwork. Boating and water safety is a key component in every junior sailing program. These lessons are widely applicable to other types of boating and recreation.
Why Learn in a Small Boat?
Jack London once quipped that the "small boat sailor is the real sailor." Small sailboats are very responsive to weight placement, sail trim, and rudder movements. Those who master sailing a small boat develop exceptional feel and awareness. It's no wonder that most of the professional sailors in the America's Cup or Volvo Round the World Race started in 8' Optimist dinghies. The skills learned on a small boat are easily transferable to larger sailboats, while adults who learned on larger boats often find dinghy sailing very challenging.
There are about 50 learn to sail programs in Washington and Oregon. Sailing classes are taught by a variety of different organizations. Historically yacht clubs were the hub of youth sailing activities. Today a wide range of organizations are involved in sailing instruction. These range from independent non-profit sailing centers to commercial sailing schools, and even parks and recreation departments. Our geography has endowed us with many wonderful lakes, rivers, and protected harbors that are well suited to sailing instruction.
When it comes to Learn to Sail classes, community sailing centers and yacht clubs have a lot in common. Just like community sailing centers, yacht clubs offer junior sailing classes that are open to the public, though yacht club members may receive a discounted price. Because both employ instructors trained by US Sailing, the activities, curriculum, and quality of instruction between yacht clubs and community based programs is very similar. Your child can have a great experience at either a community sailing center or yacht club program. The key to any outstanding program is that it's safe, fun, and that the students are learning.
Learning to Sail is not expensive, or at least no more so than any other day camp, recreational class, or club sport activity. Community sailing centers are generally a little more affordable. For a 40-hour course, the cost is typically around $300-400. When you break that down, most programs cost between $7.50-$10.00 per hour of class time. That's cheaper than a baby sitter!
Many community sailing programs and yacht clubs offer scholarships for sailors to attend class. The criteria vary from program to program, but most believe that financial circumstance is no reason to miss out. In support of this, The Sailing Foundation grants scholarships for youth sailors in Washington and Oregon who qualify for the Free/Reduced Lunch Program.
What is a Learn to Sail Program Like?
Qualified instructors, good equipment, diverse class offerings, and affordability will make your experience a positive one. Proximity is usually the main reason for choosing a program, but aside from convenience there are some other factors you should carefully consider.
1) Does the Program Hire US Sailing Certified Instructors?
US Sailing Certified Level One Instructors have to pass a rigorous course through US Sailing which is the national governing body of sailing. Having a certified instructor means they have met national standards in safety, instruction, and are familiar with the US Sailing Curriculum. Certified instructors must also hold valid CPR/First Aid certs and a state approved boating license.
2) What's after Learn to Sail?
Programs tend to be either recreational or racing in nature. The first couple years of sailing are spent working on the fundamentals, but after a child masters the basics there are many paths from which to choose. Larger keel boats, STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, & Math) education, adventure sailing, boat building, windsurfing, or paddle sports are just a few examples of recreational pathways after Learn to Sail. It's good to know what opportunities exist after mastering the basics. The best programs offer multiple classes, pathways, and levels to keep sailors engaged and on the water.
3) Do They Offer Year-Round Programming and Activities?
Most smaller programs only operate during the summer months. Others offer year round programming such as weekend "Learn to Sail," race teams, high school sailing, or open sailing. If you want to keep your child on the water during the school year ask what they have to offer in the off-season. Being able to sail 8 or 10 months a year is a huge benefit! Your child won't have to "restart" every summer and will retain more of what they learned.
4) Are They Affiliated with a Local High School or College Team?
Partnering with a local high school or university can add a wealth of vitality to a program. Having high school and college sailors around means that there is a strong dinghy sailing culture, a qualified pool of knowledgeable instructors, and activities happening throughout the year. There are also opportunities for your child to be mentored by these athletes and one day go on to sail in high school or college themselves.

content:Speaker assistant says: The most commonly used compression codec for high-resolution video is H.265 (also known as HEVC or High-Efficiency Video Coding). This codec is designed specifically for ultra-high definition (UHD) and 4K resolution video, and it offers much better compression efficiency than its predecessor, H.264. 

HEVC is the preferred codec for high-resolution video because it can reduce file sizes by up to 50% while maintaining the same level of video quality. This makes it ideal for streaming high-resolution video over the internet, where bandwidth limitations can be a concern. Additionally, HEVC supports 10-bit color depth, which allows for a wider range of colors and more accurate color representation in high dynamic range (HDR) video. 

Overall, H.265/HEVC is the best compression codec for high-resolution video because it strikes a balance between video quality and file size, making it easier to distribute and stream high-quality content over various platforms. context:The content explains that while streaming services prefer H.265/HEVC for efficient high-resolution video distribution, it introduces hardware limitations on older devices that may require transcoding or result in playback issues. keywords: H.265, video compression, HEVC tags: high_resolution_optimization, codec_selection, video_compression_standards, media_quality_assessment, device_compatibility, transcoding_necessity, device_limitations, hardware_requirements

content:Speaker user says: What are some effective practices for designing game tutorials for educational games, and how can they make games more scalable and effective?
Generate according to: Interactive learning activities, where multiple participants collaboratively generate new ideas, have been shown to produce the highest learning gains. However, interactive learning activities are often the most difficult for instructors to implement. My research explores how technology can impact how students interact during class, and how those interactions affect student learning.
This project explores ways to improve peer feedback on student presentations. Many college courses require students to give in-class presentations. This raises a number of challenges. Students who watch the presentation are typically not participating actively. Professors can be overwhelmed trying to provide feedback while also managing the class. The presenting students would benefit from receiving more feedback than the professor can provide. This project introduces PeerPresents, an in-class peer feedback system we developed to improve the feedback process for in-class presentations. PeerPresents also serves as a digital platform for investigating how technology can support interactive learning activities during in-class peer feedback exchange.
(submitted to CHI 2019) How Guiding Questions Facilitate Feedback Exchange in Project-Based Learning.
What if students can learn just as much by watching someone else play an educational game as they would by playing the game themselves? This project investigates possibilities for streaming educational games on Twitch.tv, including how much students learn by watching, what the streamer should or shouldn’t do to encourage learning, and how chat interactions affect students watching the game.
Professional game design teams sometimes struggle to implement effective processes for getting helpful feedback on their games and prototypes. This project investigates common problems in giving, receiving, and making use of feedback in the game design process through interviews with designers, managers, artists, and other game design industry professionals. This data could lead to the development of research-backed strategies for managing common problems and improving feedback processes in game design companies.
Student game designers use playtests to get frequent feedback on their games. However, student designers often don’t know what kind of feedback to ask for, and student feedback providers often need guidance to provide helpful feedback. The EOTA method scaffolds the feedback process by first encouraging those who played the game to share their experiences, then inviting those who watched the game to share what they observed, then asking all playtesters to offer theories that might explain what in the game caused those experiences or observations. Finally, playtesters may offer advice to the game design team.
(in press – Meaningful Play 2018) EOTA: A Method for Improving Peer Feedback in the Game Design Classroom.
Interactive learning techniques such as role-play are valuable to learners, but often difficult for instructors to implement. While technology can successfully support interactive learning, few systems have been designed or studied that support classroom role-play specifically. This research explores how role-play games (RPGs) can inform the design of systems to support role-play for interactive learning. Early findings reveal how role-player’s expertise – both in supporting group cohesion and in preserving the spirit of the experience – can offer instructors and system designers new insights on using role-play to support interactive learning in the classroom.
If you look to popular media, the aftermath of a natural disaster leaves behind helpless victims, selfish looters, and violent thugs. This narrative is pervasive in fiction, with the protagonists often cast as the only heroes with meaningful agency. However, it is equally pervasive in nonfiction media, such as news coverage of natural disasters. These beliefs, known as “disaster myths,” are not accurate. In fact, survivors typically care for one another, share resources, and build community in the aftermath of disaster. Why does the narrative of life after disaster matter? Because it affects policy. This work presents a case study of Pause, a game designed to change player beliefs about how people behave in the wake of a natural disaster, using metaphor as the key belief change strategy.
The traditional introductory computer science course generally consists of lectures filled with pre-coded examples. However, “live-coding”, the process of solving code examples that begins with a blank text file and requires students to produce code during lecture as a group discussion,gives students an interactive educational experience with little additional effort for the professor. Building on the flipped classroom movement, live-coding provides students with practice generating code, testing code, understanding and solving errors, and finding optimal code solutions during class. This work presents an initial evaluation of live-coding in a college level introductory computer science course.

This work synthesized a system of effective practices for the design of educational game tutorials, and demonstrated their efficacy in a new tutorial system for an educational puzzle game called BeadLoom Game (BLG).
